study: Cost of the fused-dot finiteness guard: below measurement resolution
scope: Isolated Q5_K matvec, nout=16000, nin=1024, six threads, 60 iterations per sample, six alternating pairs per session. tools/kernel_bench.cpp.

sessions.arms: guard inlined vs guard noinline, direct

finding: The three sessions are mutually inconsistent. Session 1 put the guard at -8.50% with a clean 0/6 sweep, which looked decisive. Session 3 then showed inlined and noinline forms are indistinguishable at 3/6, and session 2 put the noinline form at only -2.23%. If inline and noinline are the same, session 1 and session 2 cannot both be right. Absolute rates also moved between sessions (16.74, 13.69, 17.11 for comparable arms), so the instrument drifts more than the effect being measured.
conclusion: The guard's cost is below this instrument's resolution at this shape: somewhere between zero and a few percent, not the 8.5% that a single 6/6 sweep suggested. A 0/6 or 6/6 result is not sufficient evidence when between-session drift exceeds the effect.
action: The noinline attribute was reverted. It earned nothing measurable and added platform-specific ifdefs, which AGENTS' lean rule does not support. The guard itself stays: it is a correctness requirement, not an optimization, and its cost is within noise either way.
limits: One quant type, one shape, one machine, one thread count. Between-session variance was not separately characterised with an A/A at this shape, which is what would be needed to state a real bound rather than 'below resolution'.
